blocks.text: And since it is found to be the producer of many eggs, it (is said) to separate from the brood those that are impure, and to nourish with the flowing cylinders as many chicks as the heat has hatched. So he calls, very improperly, the wind-eggs, whose fluid, and the shell flowing away, nourish the chicks. Damir: يقال انها تقسم بيضها ثلاثا فمنه ما تحضنه ومنه ما تجعل صغارة غذ ومنه ما تفتحه وتجعله في الهوا حتي يتعفن ويتولد دودا فتتغذي به فراخها اذا خرجت من البيض [yuqāl annahā taqsim bayḍahā thalāthan fa-minhu mā taḥḍunuhu wa-minhu mā tajʿal ṣighāra ghadh wa-minhu mā taftaḥuhu wa-tajʿaluhu fī al-hawā ḥattī yataʿaffan wa-yatawallad dūdan fa-tataghadhdhī bihi firākhuhā idhā kharajat min al-bayḍ] It is said to divide its eggs into three parts, so that some of them are those on which it sits; some also, from whose yolk it is fed; and some, finally, which it opens and exposes to the air until they rot and worms are produced from them, by which its chicks are fed when they have been hatched from the egg. Alkazuinius: واذا باضت يبيض عشرين بيضة او اكثر فيجعلها ثلاثة اقسام تدفن ثلثها في التراب وتترك ثلثها في الشمس وتخضن ثلثها فاذا اخرجت فراخها كسرت ما كان في الشمس وغذتها بما فيها من الرطوبة التي ذوبتها الشمس ورقتها فاذا اشتدت فراخها وقويت اخرجت المدفون وفتحت لها ثقبا فتجمع عليها الذباب والبق والنمل وغيرها من فرعت فغذت تقوي ان الي فراخها فتاكلها الهوام [wa-idhā bāḍat yabīḍ ʿishrīn bayḍa aw akthar fa-yajʿaluhā thalāthat aqsām tadfin thuluthahā fī al-turāb wa-tatruk thuluthahā fī al-shams wa-takhḍin thuluthahā fa-idhā akhrajat firākhahā kasarat mā kāna fī al-shams wa-ghadhdhathā bi-mā fīhā min al-ruṭūba allatī dhawwabathā al-shams wa-raqqathā fa-idhā ishtaddat firākhuhā wa-qawiyat akhrajat al-madfūn wa-fataḥat lahā thuqban fa-tajammaʿ ʿalayhā al-dhubāb wa-al-baqq wa-al-naml wa-ghayruhā min frʿt fghdht tqwy an ilā firākhihā fa-taʾkuluhā al-hawāmm] [col. 258] When it lays eggs — and it lays twenty or more — it divides them into three parts: one of these it buries in the earth, one it exposes to the sun, and on one it sits. And when the chicks have hatched, it breaks the part that was in the sun and feeds the chicks with the fluid they contain, [II, 864] after it has been liquefied and softened by the sun. And when the chicks grow strong and sturdy, it digs up the buried eggs and pierces them, so that flies, bugs, ants and similar little creatures gather to them, on which the chicks feed until, having become stronger, they run and feed themselves. But these things are closer to fables, since they attribute to the animal not only prudence but also foresight; yet that it is most stupid will be evident from what I am about to say.

1. Other animals choose foods suited to their nature; this one devours without any discrimination whatever presents itself: iron, bones, glass, stones, clods of earth, coals, glowing embers, gems hanging from the ears of bystanders; and it is said not only to swallow these but also to digest them. Pliny, book 10, chapter 1: Of a wondrous nature in digesting what it has devoured without discrimination. Aelian, book 14, chapter 7, says that stones are found in the belly of a slain one, ὥσπερ οὖν καταπιοῦσα ἡ στρουθὸς ἐν τῷ ἐχίνῳ φυλάττει, καὶ πέττει τῷ χρόνῳ [hōsper oun katapiousa hē strouthos en tō echinō phylattei, kai pettei tō chronō], which, having swallowed them and kept them in its omasum, it at length digests. Porta coeli fol. 22. d.: כתב אבן רשד כי בהלעיטה את הזהב הוא נתך בגופה מחמם יותר מן האש בסגולה שלהם, Averroës wrote that it melts swallowed gold in its body, as if it were hotter than fire, through a property implanted in it. Alkazuinius: ياكل الحصاة فتذوب في قانصته حتي يصير كالما بالخاصية خلقها الله فيه [yaʾkul al-ḥaṣāh fa-tadhūb fī qāniṣatihi ḥattī yaṣīr ka-l-mā bi-l-khāṣṣiyya khalaqahā allāh fīhi] It devours stones and melts them in its stomach until they become like water, through a faculty placed in it by God. And a little later: وايضا يبلع الجمر ولا يضرها [wa-ayḍan yablaʿ al-jamr wa-lā yaḍurruhā] It also devours coals, which do it no harm. Likewise: وتحمي صنجة ماية دينار من الحديد حتي تحمر وترمي الي النعامة فتبلعها وتسترها [wa-tuḥmā ṣanjat māyat dīnār min al-ḥadīd ḥattā taḥmarr wa-turmā ilā al-naʿāma fa-tablaʿuhā wa-tasturuhā] And an iron weight of a hundred denarii is heated until red-hot and thrown to the ostrich, which devours it and stores it away. So also Damir: وتتبلع العظم الصلب والحجر والمدر والحديد وتذيبه ^{d)} كالماء [wa-tatabalaʿ al-ʿaẓm al-ṣulb wa-al-ḥajar wa-al-madar wa-al-ḥadīd wa-tudhībuhu ^{d)} ka-l-māʾ] And it devours hard bones, and stones, and clods, and iron, which it liquefies like water. Likewise: واذا رات في اذن صغير لولوة خطفتها [wa-idhā raʾat fī udhn ṣaghīr luʾluʾa khaṭifathā] And when it sees a small pearl in an ear, it snatches it. And again: وتتبلع الجمر فيكون جوفها هو العامل في اطفايه [II, 865] ولا يكون الجمر عاملا في احراقة وفي ذلك اعجوبتان احدا [col. 259] هما التغذي بما لا يتغذي به والثانية الاستمرا والهضم [wa-tatabalaʿ al-jamr fa-yakūn jawfuhā huwa al-ʿāmil fī iṭfāyih [II, 865] wa-lā yakūn al-jamr ʿāmilan fī iḥrāqih wa-fī dhālika uʿjūbatān aḥad [col. 259] humā al-taghadhdhī bi-mā lā yutaghadhdhā bihi wa-al-thāniya al-istimrā wa-al-haḍm] It also swallows embers, and its body is effective in extinguishing them, but the embers are not effective in burning it. In this there is a double marvel: one, that it is nourished by things that do not nourish; the other, their digestion and concoction. So they say, but, as usual, hyperbolically exaggerated. Aelian says stones are found in its belly which it has swallowed and digested, which is a remarkable ἐναντιολογία [enantiologia]. Alexander of Aphrodisias, in the Preface to Aristotle's Problems, expressly denies that iron is digested by the ostrich. And Albertus asserts that the stones it has greedily devoured it afterwards spits out, that is, ejects through the mouth. And Ulysses Aldrovandi says it swallows bits of iron which it excretes again undigested. And Gesner, after saying that it devours whatever it touches, linen, iron, stones, says: But these remain undigested and whole in its stomach. And if they are too many, they finally bring the animal to death or to wasting, as has appeared in dissected ones.
